newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London closed broadly lower on producer selling and light fund liquidation. However, late industry buying helped values to end off the day's lows. November shed $17 to close at $1,488 a tonne. Other positions were $6 to $20 lower.

In New York arabica futures closed lower hurt by steady speculative liquidation and a dearth of industry buying. An early sell-off was triggered in part by the latest commitment of traders data showing an unexpected large net speculative long position. December slid 2.30 cents/lb to close at 102,95 cents/lb, while March lost 1.90 cents/lb to close at 99.50 cents/lb. The back months lost between 1.05 to 2.00 cents/lb.

US certified coffee stocks for delivery at the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange fell sharply during the week ended September 27, which should boost prices on Tuesday as the draw down caught many operators by surprise. Equally important is the absence of coffee awaiting certification, or approval, at exchange warehouses.
Traders said the certified stock data, coming at the start of the 1996/97 harvest in key Latin American producing countries, could boost December's already steep premium to outer months.
UNITED STATES - Certified coffee stocks for delivery at the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange fell sharply by 10,433 bags to 31,669 bags during the week ended September 27.

Stocks in New York remained unchanged at 4,811 bags while stocks in New Orleans fell by 8,346 bags to 18,644 bags (26,990 bags). Stocks in Miami fell by 2,337 bags (-1,065 bags) to 2,214 bags (4,551 bags) while stocks in San Francisco increased by 250 bags (+500 bags) to 6,000 bags (5,750 bags).
The drawdown reduced the CSCE stockpile to at least a ten-year low, traders said, although exact historical comparisons were not immediately available from the exchange.

UNITED STATES - Coffee roastings for the week ended September 21, totalled approximately 290,000 60-kg bags, down from 345,000 bags in the previous week and compared with 300,000 bags in the corresponding week one year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 12.275 million bags vs 12.000 million bags the same year-ago period.

CANADA - Canada imported 239,586 bags of coffee in April 1996, 22 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 899,900 bags, nearly 17 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 11 per cent to 2.510 million bags.
Major suppliers of green coffee in January/April 1996 were Mexico (105,600 vs 45,700 bags) and Colombia (163,200 vs 113,000 bags).

The country exported 106,500 bags of coffee in January/April 1996, 9 per cent less than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 9.2 per cent to 303,800 bags.

INDIA - According to India's state-run Coffee Board coffee production in 1996/97 (October/September) is likely to fall to 3.662 million 60-kg bags, down from 3.716 million bags produced in 1995/96. The 1996/97 figure comprises 1.626 million bags arabicas and 2.036 million bags robustas which compares to 1.720 million bags and 1.996 million bags respectively last season.

Commerce Minister B.B. Ramaiah said that the government could impose a ban on coffee exports or allow imports if necessary to ensure domestic supply and stable prices. Earlier this month, the federal government freed the coffee trade from controls, allowing growers to directly market all their produce without surrendering part of it to the state-run Coffee Board as in the past. This has raised fears that the freeing of the coffee trade would lead to unchecked exports and a domestic coffee shortage.
